content:
Quick answer: These smoothie recipes are food ideas, not treatments for arthritis or a promise of less joint pain. Keep taking prescribed medicines and follow your care plan. NHS advice is to limit fruit or vegetable juice and smoothies to a combined total of 150ml a day, with meals.

Five smoothie ideas using everyday ingredients

The ingredient lists below make larger batches, not a recommended single serving. Blend until smooth and divide into small portions. Adjust flavour or thickness to taste, and check ingredients for allergies or dietary restrictions. There is no need to add supplements.

1. Beetroot and berry smoothie

  • 1 small cooked beetroot (peeled, chopped)
  • 1 cup frozen mixed berries
  • 1 banana
  • 1-inch fresh ginger, grated
  • 1 cup almond milk
  • 1 tbsp ground flaxseed

Blend the ingredients and divide into small portions. These ingredients are included for food and flavour, not a measured therapeutic effect.

2. Mango and turmeric smoothie

  • 1 frozen banana
  • 1 cup mango chunks
  • 1 tsp turmeric powder
  • Pinch of black pepper, optional for flavour
  • 1 tbsp coconut oil
  • 1 cup oat milk

Blend the ingredients and divide into small portions. These ingredients are included for food and flavour, not a measured therapeutic effect.

3. Green apple and spinach smoothie

  • 2 handfuls spinach
  • 1 green apple
  • 1/2 avocado
  • Juice of 1 lemon
  • 1-inch fresh ginger
  • 1 cup water
  • 1 tbsp chia seeds

Blend the ingredients and divide into small portions. These ingredients are included for food and flavour, not a measured therapeutic effect.

4. Cherry and yoghurt smoothie

  • 1 cup frozen tart cherries
  • 1 banana
  • 1 cup Greek yoghurt
  • 1 tbsp honey
  • 1/2 cup pomegranate juice

Blend the ingredients and divide into small portions. These ingredients are included for food and flavour, not a measured therapeutic effect.

5. Blueberry, walnut and kefir smoothie

  • 1 cup frozen blueberries
  • 2 tbsp walnuts
  • 1 tbsp hemp seeds
  • 1 tbsp ground flaxseed
  • 1 cup kefir
  • 1 tsp cinnamon

Blend the ingredients and divide into small portions. These ingredients are included for food and flavour, not a measured therapeutic effect.

Portion size and teeth

NHS advice is to limit fruit juice, vegetable juice and smoothies to a combined total of 150ml a day. Crushing fruit releases sugars that can damage teeth. Have smoothies with a meal rather than sipping them between meals. A larger batch should not be treated as a daily serving.

Are these anti-inflammatory treatments?

No. Nutrients and plant compounds are studied in different settings, but that does not establish that these particular recipes reduce arthritis symptoms. A smoothie cannot replace your medicines, exercise advice or other care. Use it as one food choice within a varied diet, not as a daily treatment you have to follow.

Medicines, allergies and individual needs

These recipes include ingredients such as nuts, milk or dairy alternatives, seeds, ginger and turmeric. Check allergies, product labels and your own dietary advice. If you have been given a specific diet or fluid restriction, ask your clinician or dietitian how the recipes fit. Concentrated supplements are different from culinary ingredients; check any supplement with a pharmacist before combining it with medicines.

Questions people ask

Do I need black pepper with turmeric?

Not for this recipe. Add it only if you like the flavour. This is not an attempt to reproduce a curcumin supplement trial, and greater supplement absorption is not automatically safer.

Should I replace meals with smoothies?

These recipes are not designed as complete meal replacements or personalised nutrition plans. If eating or maintaining weight is difficult, ask your GP or dietitian for advice.

See the arthritis diet guide and ginger and turmeric evidence and safety guide for context. General information only, not personal medical advice.
